title: bn254-pairing-inversion: gated tag-walk rho (a walk step is an inner product on 64-bit words), expected work, output ([x]P0, Q0)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, g=e(P0,Q0), the algorithm in proof.md returns P=[x]P0 in G1 and Q=Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z (for z=1: P=infinity and Q=Q0) with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (an opened run that is never capped finds x after at most 107/100 times sqrt(pi r m/(2(m-1))) walk steps in expectation, m=6), H2 (averaged over runs, the elements evaluated for the first time fall in the distinguished set and in the uncertified tag sets at most a stated factor more often than the sizes of those sets) and H3 (at most 2^98 evaluations of already visited elements in expectation), supported by a proved tag lemma, algebra on the pinned constants and full-algorithm toy runs. Before any other work the algorithm reads one fresh 64-bit coin u and opens the run only when u < K, K = 7229537559736918267, the least integer for which the opened share of runs times the supported success of an opened run reaches 0.39; a closed run costs 64 instructions and is counted as a failure. An opened run finds x by a sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho walk in GT with 6 multipliers g^c z^d: the next multiplier is read from one stored coordinate of the current element, a step computes a 64-bit tag as the inner product of 60 stored 51-bit digits with 60 table words, refines it with a second inner product when it is too close to a boundary, and uses a tag only when it certifies the exact selector (proof.md section 2), the table holds every product of at most 1,250 multipliers, one Fp12 product re-bases the element every 1,250 steps, uncertified elements are evaluated exactly, distinguished elements (90 bits) go to an ordered store keyed by the whole element, and g^x=z is checked before output; it continues until it finds x or a counter reaches its cap. The score is an expectation: the expected total computation over the same uniform challenges and fresh coins is at most 2^118.863948 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000). It is not a bound on every run: on every run the total computation is at most 2^129.347893 equivalents, enforced by counters (a trip budget of 1,251 per call of the step loop, a 3-word exit counter compared with its cap at every exit, 2^50 walk starts, 2^50 reports, 16 recoveries). Prices are executed instruction counts of generated AArch64 programs: 121 instructions per walk step, 178 more for a second-level tag, and 15,135 per exit from the step loop (one Fp12 product of 13,843 with the label additions, digits and counters, plus a stated allowance). Both totals include the gate, all input checks, constants, the table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), walk starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification, the scalar multiplication and pairing check of the output. Peak memory is at most 2^62.877284 bytes in one address space with 64-bit pointers; preprocessing is at most 2^57.970905 equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, the walk's step loop on real windows, the re-base with its counters on both sides of both caps, both tag levels, both sides of both certificate thresholds, the trip budget) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check both tag lemmas and the certified-selector corollary on production-size values; recompute every ledger integer, the gate constant K (and that K - 1 fails), the expected and every-run totals and the score; execute the output step P=[x]P0; run the complete algorithm of proof.md to its output in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
